clue.text: Marx on the means to puncture a spouter

definitions.text: the means to puncture a spouter

parts.note: Harpo was the silent, harp-playing one of the Marx Brothers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Somebody sets one of the Marx Brothers on the job of stabbing a loudmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'spouter' sounds like a windbag orator, but here it is a whale, which spouts water from its blowhole.
explanation.definitionFit: A whaler's barbed spear is the tool thrown to pierce a whale.

clue.text: Mr Punch's intuitions

explanation.surface: The puppet Mr Punch's gut feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Punch of the Punch and Judy puppet show is humpbacked, carrying humps; and gut feelings are intuitions.

clue.text: Bank people have their knife into old heretics

parts.note: to rip is to slash with a blade
the Arians followed Arius, who denied the full divinity of Christ in the 4th century

explanation.surface: Bankers are out to get some ancient heretics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank people' looks like bankers; it means people living on a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Riparian means of a riverbank, and riparians are those who own or live on river banks.

clue.text: So thy martyred saint is in Essex

indicators.note: martyred, as in tortured, signals the two words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An Essex saint who died for her faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Martyred' reads as part of the saint's story but is the anagram signal on SO THY.
explanation.definitionFit: St Osyth was an Anglo-Saxon princess killed by raiders, and a village in Essex bears her name.

clue.text: It takes a girl keen for cotton to flourish in U.S.

annotationWithheld.why: It takes a girl keen for cotton to flourish in U.S. (9): NAN + TUCKET (flourish) with nankeen (cotton) read from 'girl keen'; 'keen' is both part of the cotton and the piece replaced, and 'It' / 'in U.S.' split the definition
annotationWithheld.clue: It takes a girl keen for cotton to flourish in U.S.

clue.text: Arab craft put ashore the lutenist

parts.note: a dow (more often spelt dhow) is an Arab sailing vessel
to land people or goods is to put them ashore

explanation.surface: An Arab boat sets a musician down on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dowland was the great Elizabethan composer and player of the lute.

clue.text: Fate cannot harm me, I have —— today" (Sydney Smith)

definitions.text: Fate cannot harm me, I have —— today" (Sydney Smith)

parts.words: Fate cannot harm me, I have —— today" (Sydney Smith)
parts.note: the line comes from Sydney Smith's comic Recipe for a Salad, ending in contentment after a good meal

explanation.surface: A line from the clergyman-wit Sydney Smith with a word left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Smith's salad verse ends 'Fate cannot harm me, I have dined today', a well-fed man's contentment.

clue.text: Lee's defence work

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side away from the wind, though Lee also suggests the Confederate general's fortifications

explanation.surface: General Robert E. Lee's fortifications in the American Civil War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lee' looks like the Civil War general; it is the lee, the side sheltered from the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge or fence planted to shelter ground from gusts makes a sheltered lee side.

clue.text: One in stormy Lear spirited into another storm

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the rearranged letters
stormy signals that the king's name is tossed into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A character from the storm scene in King Lear is whisked into another stormy play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormy' anagrams LEAR to AREL, and 'in' puts I inside. The other storm is The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy spirit who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: Distressed lady a horse from dawn to dusk

indicators.note: distressed means battered, so the word lady is knocked into a new order

parts.note: a- means on, as in astride, and a horse is a gee, written G, so on a gee

explanation.surface: An upset woman spends the whole day on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distressed' anagrams LADY to DAYL; 'a-horse' (printed hyphenated) is ON + G, a gee being a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting the whole day runs from sunrise to nightfall.

clue.text: "Heady" — though not headwear for baby

explanation.surface: A word glossed as heady, with a note that it is not something a baby wears on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic 'head' in 'headwear' points at the second sense: a baby's garment, worn at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Old ale called heady was strong and foaming; and the infant's cloth worn round the bottom is no hat.

clue.text: A Pooter

parts.note: Charles Pooter is the self-important clerk of the comic novel The Diary of a Nobody, so a Pooter is a nobody

explanation.surface: A lone name offered as the definition of a type of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooter is the hero of The Diary of a Nobody, so his name stands for a person of no importance.

clue.text: Herbal cough cure for ageing member of the pack, say ?

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase before it is to be heard spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: an ageing hound turns hoar, that is grey-haired, so a hoar hound

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy for an old dog's cough.
explanation.walkthrough: HOAR (grey with age) plus HOUND (a member of a hunting pack) is spoken the same as the name of the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: The bitter herb is made into a syrup or sweet traditionally taken for coughs.

clue.text: Note, one pound weight, no more, of sharp steel

parts.note: B is a musical note
I is the Roman numeral for one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
O, a nought, is nothing more

explanation.surface: A bill for a pound's weight of sharp steel, with nothing extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A bilbo is an old sword, named after Bilbao, famous for its blades.

clue.text: Well-groomed poet

explanation.surface: A dapper poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart dress is neat and stylish; and Christopher Smart was the 18th-century poet of Jubilate Agno.

clue.text: Walk, philosopher, to work perforce

parts.note: to tread is to walk
John Stuart Mill was the Victorian philosopher of liberty

explanation.surface: A philosopher is made to walk to work.
explanation.walkthrough: The prison treadmill made convicts tread a wheel as forced labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill was a prison wheel convicts were compelled to tread, so labour done under compulsion.

clue.text: Norfolk rebel heading for this Midland town and nearly going wrong

parts.note: Robert Kett led the Norfolk rising of 1549; heading places him at the front

indicators.note: nearly says the word for going wrong is not quite complete, lacking one letter

parts.note: erring means going wrong

explanation.surface: A rebel from Norfolk marches on a Midlands town and nearly loses his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for' reads as a march on the town but puts the rebel first; 'nearly' takes one R from ERRING, leaving ERING.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettering is a town in Northamptonshire, in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Convert a profit, a future Lord Mayor was urged

definitions.text: a future Lord Mayor was urged

parts.note: to turn something is to convert it
gain means profit

explanation.surface: Advice to make a profit given to a man who will one day be Lord Mayor.
explanation.walkthrough: In the legend, Bow Bells told Dick Whittington 'Turn again, Whittington, Lord Mayor of London'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bells called back the young Whittington, later Lord Mayor of London, with the words 'Turn again'.

clue.text: Kinda inn I find refurbished for his Nibs

definitions.note: for pen nibs, playing on 'his nibs', a mock title for a self-important man

indicators.note: refurbished means done up anew, so these letters are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone finds a kind of inn renovated for a self-important gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His Nibs' looks like a mocking title; it is pen nibs, which this black drawing ink fills.
explanation.definitionFit: This dense black ink is used with dip pens, whose nibs carry it.

clue.text: Chapel-goer welcomed to urban Norfolk

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk
a visitor welcomed to the house is told 'Enter!'

explanation.surface: A chapel-goer is given a warm welcome in a Norfolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: The welcome 'Enter!' comes after the town's name in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonconformists who worshipped in chapels rather than the Church of England were called dissenters.

clue.text: Burke's rival ?

parts.note: Burke's Peerage is a guide to the British aristocracy, with one long-standing competitor

explanation.surface: A rival of the statesman Edmund Burke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burke' suggests the 18th-century politician Edmund Burke; it is Burke's Peerage, the guide to titled families.
explanation.definitionFit: Debrett's Peerage competes with Burke's Peerage as the reference book on the British nobility.

clue.text: Credit for a bed in the botanical gardens ? It's not unheard of

indicators.note: not unheard means it is heard, so the phrase before is to be taken by its sound

parts.words: a bed in the botanical gardens
parts.note: Kew is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London, and a doss is a rough bed, so a Kew doss

explanation.surface: Someone seeks credit for a flowerbed at Kew, and claims the idea is not unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bed in the botanical gardens' looks like a flowerbed; it is a doss (a place to sleep) at Kew, London's botanic gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is praise or prestige earned for an achievement.

clue.text: Ready to be backed in the race

definitions.text: Ready to be backed in the race

parts.words: Ready to be backed in the race
parts.note: a racehorse ready to be ridden has its riding seat fitted, and backed also means bet on

explanation.surface: A horse ready for punters to put money on in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' looks like betting; here it means mounted by a rider, which first needs the seat strapped on.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse fitted with its riding seat is ready to be mounted.

clue.text: A proprietary fuel being consumed

explanation.surface: A branded fuel going up in flames.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name is a proprietary label; and a burning piece of wood is a firebrand.

clue.text: So youth answered the call, and one near-late new arrival

definitions.text: So youth answered the call, and one near-late new arrival

parts.words: So youth answered the call, and one near-late new arrival
parts.note: the Latin reply 'I am present' given by schoolboys at roll call, and by Thackeray's Colonel Newcome as he died

explanation.surface: How a boy answered the roll call, and how someone arriving just in time did too.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Newcomes, Colonel Newcome dies saying the word he used at school roll call; 'near-late' is the pupil who arrives just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Adsum is Latin for 'I am here', the reply to a called register.

clue.text: Applaud those who run the company for being so wooden

definitions.note: an adjective here, as in a clapboard house

parts.note: to clap is to applaud
the board of directors run a company

explanation.surface: Praising company directors for their stiff performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden' looks like a theatre critic's put-down of the board; it defines timber weatherboarding.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapboard is overlapping timber boarding cladding a building, so a clapboard house is made of planks.

clue.text: A Spanish hero hesitates to drink it

parts.note: El Cid is the medieval Castilian warrior-hero
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A Spanish hero pauses before taking a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hesitates to drink' paints a reluctant drinker, but the hesitation is only the filler sound; El Cid is the 11th-century Castilian champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic drink of fermented apple juice.

clue.text: Twice mounted a beast

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used as an encore call
a rider mounted is on the horse

explanation.surface: Someone rides an animal two times.
explanation.definitionFit: The bison is a large wild ox of the American plains and European forests.

clue.text: Company of John

parts.note: John Company was the popular nickname of the trading firm that ruled much of India

explanation.surface: The firm belonging to a man named John.
explanation.definitionFit: The British trading company that governed India until 1858 was nicknamed John Company.

clue.text: Eat an' so drink deep to Samuel Slumkey?

definitions.text: Eat an' so drink deep to Samuel Slumkey?

parts.words: Eat an' so drink deep to Samuel Slumkey?
parts.note: in Dickens's Pickwick Papers Samuel Slumkey stands for Parliament at the borough of ...; the word that completes 'Eat an'' also means drink deeply

explanation.surface: An invitation to eat and drink heavily in honour of a parliamentary candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: Eatanswill is the rowdy election town in Pickwick Papers; adding the answer to 'Eat an'' gives it, and the answer alone means guzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To swill is to gulp a drink greedily, and it ends the name of the Dickensian borough.

clue.text: Knight or Saint

explanation.surface: Two titles offered as alternatives.
explanation.definitionFit: The Knights Templar were a crusading military order; and Simon Templar is the gentleman thief nicknamed the Saint.

clue.text: No slippers? That's sure tiring

parts.note: the slippers are things that slide, and tiring means fitting with tyres, so it describes grippy tyres

explanation.surface: Someone without slippers complains of fatigue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiring' sounds like fatigue but means fitting tyres; 'slippers' are not footwear but things that slide.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyres with a tread pattern that grips the road stop a car skidding.
